vision.paraphrase: Sorting transactions into categories with rules written once is the second goal.

conops.paraphrase: The user writes rules.txt and runs categorize; every transaction gets a category.

vision.paraphrase: Simple rules need a simple tie-break the user can predict: the order they wrote them in.

conops.paraphrase: Each transaction gets the category of the first rule that matches.

vision.paraphrase: Every transaction must land somewhere so totals stay complete.

conops.paraphrase: Transactions no rule matches are uncategorized.

requirements.rationale: Banks vary case and spacing between exports; matching must tolerate that, but the stored text is the user's evidence and is never tidied.

vision.paraphrase: Rules interpret the description without changing what is stored: the ledger stays a faithful record.

conops.paraphrase: Matching ignores how the bank capitalised or spaced the text; the description is left exactly as stored.

vision.paraphrase: Rules the user writes once must exist before categories can be assigned; the tool says so plainly.

conops.paraphrase: Without rules.txt the user is told what is missing and what to do.
